scope: Docs-only final-title aliases for current boxes tests. These existing owners were already audited; no baseline count, test execution, disposition count or source code changes are introduced.
countTreatment: Aliases only; never add these entries to original or incoming test counts.

entries.finalName: device tool installation uses the lockfile without dependency lifecycle scripts

originalOwner.name: the device tools install the pinned versions from the shipped lockfile without lifecycle scripts

sixBar.independentContract: Device cache installations use the pinned lockfile and disable dependency lifecycle scripts (Devices phase2 fleet §5 and npm security invocation).
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: The emitted installer loses npm ci or --ignore-scripts, allowing lockfile drift or package lifecycle execution in the runner.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal native npm ci and --ignore-scripts command bytes; no expectation is obtained from tool version metadata.
sixBar.stableSeam: The shipped device-tools shell artifact supplied to the generated cache workflow.
sixBar.refactorResistance: No TypeScript symbol, helper count, generated hash or whole-program snapshot is asserted; this is the explicitly retained security-relevant native command-byte guard.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Package installer tests own lock/staging/idempotency; this owner uniquely verifies the security flag reaches the generated cache-warming artifact.

entries.finalName: the Android cache installs the x86_64 API 35 image and SDK tools

originalOwner.name: the Android cache holds the API 35 x86_64 image and the default Pixel profiles, from the box host's pinned cmdline-tools

sixBar.independentContract: The Linux x64 cache ships platform-tools, emulator and the API35 Google APIs x86_64 system image required by rented Android hosts (Devices phase2 fleet §5).
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: Missing SDK tools or a wrong system-image ABI/API prevents a restored rented host from starting its default Android emulator.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal public SDK package IDs platform-tools, emulator and system-images;android-35;google_apis;x86_64.
sixBar.stableSeam: Generated Android SDK installation shell artifact; these are native sdkmanager package argument bytes.
sixBar.refactorResistance: The guard does not reference the producer package array, cmdline-tools constants, profile helpers or template snapshots; identifier-only changes preserve these protocol bytes.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Local SDK tests do not verify the GitHub cache program delivers the required remote x64 packages; workflow syntax alone cannot detect a wrong package/image ID.

entries.finalName: the iOS runner build picks the newest available iOS runtime and its newest iPhone

originalOwner.name: the iOS runner build picks the newest iOS runtime and its newest iPhone

sixBar.independentContract: The cache warmer selects the latest available iOS runtime and an iPhone compatible with it, excluding unavailable/watchOS runtimes and refusing absence (device-cache.ts public script contract).
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: Lexical version sorting, using an unavailable/newer non-iOS runtime, or picking an iPad yields the wrong native simulator creation request.
sixBar.independentOracle: Independent runtime JSON and literal iOS27.0/iPhone17-Pro identifiers recorded from the native simctl create call; an empty inventory must never request creation.
sixBar.stableSeam: Entire shipped bash program, real Node execution and an isolated xcrun dependency that stops at simulator creation.
sixBar.refactorResistance: No embedded Node expression is regex-extracted, no implementation helper calculates the expected selection, and harmless internal program restructuring preserves the recorded native request.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Workflow YAML tests cannot evaluate semantic version/device selection inside the delivered program; this is its cheapest stable native execution boundary without starting a real simulator.

entries.finalName: Linux device hosts restore their SDK and tools before the agent, without saving on cancellation

originalOwner.name: Linux boxes enable KVM before orq-agent starts; device hosts restore the Android and tool caches

sixBar.independentContract: Devices phase2 fleet §§2.6,5: prepare=devices restores Android SDK/AVDs and tools before agent start; ordinary boxes avoid device caches, cache failure is best-effort, and cancellable box runs never save.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: Wrong paths or missing/late restore causes cache misses/slow host start; a failed optional cache blocks startup; saving only on cancelled box teardown never populates caches.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal persisted SDK/AVD/tools paths, restore action, continue-on-error state, selected input conditions, restore-before-agent and absence of box save actions.
sixBar.stableSeam: Parsed actual emitted GitHub Actions workflow configuration, selected by public os/prepare inputs.
sixBar.refactorResistance: English step lists, private step names and same-producer script/key/path comparisons were removed; assertions concern required configuration effects and public path bytes.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: The cache warmer owns cache production; this owner uniquely verifies Linux box consumption, startup ordering and cancellable-run policy.

entries.finalName: macOS device hosts restore the iOS runner only for a known Xcode build

originalOwner.name: macOS device hosts restore agent-device's iOS runner keyed on the Xcode build

sixBar.independentContract: Devices phase2 fleet §5: agent-device runner caches are compatible with a specific Xcode build and can be restored only when that build is known.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: A missing build still triggers restore or the key ceases to depend on Xcode, reusing an incompatible XCTest runner.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal native runner cache path, restore action and absence when build output is unavailable; delivered key must reference a build output.
sixBar.stableSeam: Actual parsed macOS device-host GitHub workflow artifact and externally supplied step output state.
sixBar.refactorResistance: No expected renderer output, exact English step list, private xcode identifier assertion or producer key helper remains.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: The native iOS selector chooses a simulator; it cannot detect the workflow restoring an incompatible Xcode-specific build cache.

entries.finalName: the device-cache workflow saves the same SDK, tools and iOS runner keys and paths that box runs restore

originalOwner.name: the device-cache workflow builds what is missing and saves it under the keys box runs restore

sixBar.independentContract: Devices phase2 fleet §5 and actions/cache protocol: a separate warmer produces missing SDK/tools/Apple runner caches under the same per-OS keys/paths boxes consume, and hits avoid rebuilding.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: A cache is never saved, save/restore keys or paths disagree, OS branches swap tool keys, or a hit unnecessarily reinstalls/rebuilds and saves.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal expected cache-family path sets and permissions/input keys, independently compare delivered producer/consumer keys after selecting the tools OS branch, and no native install/save work for hit outputs.
sixBar.stableSeam: Both actual emitted GitHub workflows parsed as YAML, using public dispatch inputs and cache output state.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Exact step ordering, English names and private helper arrays were removed; checks retain semantic cache families, wire keys/paths and selected install/save behavior.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Box restore tests alone cannot detect cache production mismatch or unnecessary expensive rebuilds; this owner checks the complete public artifact handshake.

entries.finalName: pairing URLs use the public route and redact the secret code from logs

originalOwner.name: the pair route is exempt from user auth by its exact pattern, and its code never reaches a log line

sixBar.independentContract: BYO phase3 §2.1 and AGENTS.md: pairing uses the public /api/boxes/pair/<code> route and secrets must not be logged.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: The public route changes unexpectedly, a live pairing code leaks into logs, or unrelated agent download paths become unreadable/redacted.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal public pair URL, literal [redacted] replacement preserving query data, and unchanged public agent path.
sixBar.stableSeam: Public boxRoutes.pair URL serialization and production redactUrlTokens output.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Removed the same-constant allow-list self-check; remaining assertions protect stable user-facing URL bytes/privacy, independent of private names and observer shape.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: The hub owner separately checks the exact security exemption list; route/server tests cannot detect log-token redaction output.

entries.finalName: watchBoxDir filters events, invalidates on a link drop, and unsubscribes on close

originalOwner.name: watchBoxDir: fs.change events for its watch id reach the service; a link change re-arms

sixBar.independentContract: Box secret-file watch API: only events for the active watch reach the subscriber; losing the link invalidates it; closing unsubscribes and prevents later delivery.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: Another watcher leaks events to this subscriber, a dead link leaves stale state, or a closed subscription continues handling secret-file changes.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal .env/.env.local deliveries, ignored foreign watch ID, null invalidation plus failure receipt, and no changes after close.
sixBar.stableSeam: Production watchBoxDir handle and box filesystem event/status transport boundary.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Current title accurately states the handle contract; the caller performs re-arm, so no claim about private caller re-arm structure survives.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Host watcher tests do not protect box watch-ID multiplexing or transport disconnect invalidation; higher secret-sync service scenarios do not isolate those boundary conditions.

entries.finalName: the read-back hasher (no hash tool in the box) hashes whole files and requested prefixes

originalOwner.name: the read-back hasher (no hash tool in the box) reads each file with a length

sixBar.independentContract: Configuration sync SHA256 compatibility: fallback read-back hashing must return SHA256 of actual full/prefix bytes, with null for missing files.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: A constant/wrong digest, ignored prefix length, or false digest for a missing file corrupts incremental conflict detection.
sixBar.independentOracle: Known literal SHA256(hello)=2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824 for full hello and five-byte hello-world prefix; missing is null.
sixBar.stableSeam: execBoxHasher fallback over actual native files when no remote hash tool is available.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Removed private read-length inventory and equality of two producer outputs; literal digest and absent-file result survive hasher implementation refactors.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Native hash-tool scenarios cannot detect the no-tool read-back path; readBoxFile owns bounded reads but does not verify hashing semantics.

entries.finalName: the box copy blanks nested credential values while preserving settings that name credentials

originalOwner.name: secret paths: MCP env/headers and credential-named keys, not names of secrets

sixBar.independentContract: AGENTS.md and boxes sync security: credentials stay host-only; credential-name settings and safe CLI options remain meaningful in the delivered configuration.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: Nested API keys/MCP env/header values leak to the box, or API_KEY_ENV_VAR/apiKeyHelper/output-token options are wrongly redacted.
sixBar.independentOracle: Independent literal serialized JSON object with blank actual secret values and preserved credential-name/helper/output-limit values.
sixBar.stableSeam: syncCodec(mcp-json).toBox actual serialized output, replacing the private secretPaths inventory.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Private redaction traversal/export/call shape may change while the delivered semantic object remains correct; no expected path list is generated from the owner.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Service synchronization tests cover representative files but not these nested secret-value-versus-name distinctions; this is the lowest actual serialization boundary.

entries.finalName: baselines survive a fresh store and disappear when their box is forgotten

originalOwner.name: baselines round-trip and drop unreadable entries

sixBar.independentContract: Incremental configuration sync baselines persist across daemon/store restart and are removed when their box is forgotten.
sixBar.realRegressionDetection: The baseline only lives in memory, loses file metadata on reload, or survives box deletion and contaminates a later sync.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal hash/size/mtime metadata reloaded through a new BoxSyncBaselines instance, followed by empty state through another fresh instance after forget.
sixBar.stableSeam: Public baseline store get/markDirty/flush/forget operations and real temporary durable files.
sixBar.refactorResistance: Title no longer claims unarranged unreadable entries; actual disk round-trip and delete semantics are independent of in-memory representation and helper layout.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Service-level restart cases cannot cheaply isolate baseline metadata serialization and explicit per-box forget; config-change store tests own a different durable record format.
